paths.title: Concert / contemporary company dancer
paths.what: You dance full seasons with a company that makes its own repertory and performs it in theaters and on tour.
paths.how_in: Most dancers get in through a company's school, summer intensive, trainee program or second company, then get pulled up; open company auditions exist but are few and competitive.
paths.training: Years of daily technique (ballet plus modern/contemporary). Some go to a BFA program first, others go straight from a trainee or second company. No degree is strictly required.
paths.pay: $24.80 an hour (BLS median for all dancers, May 2025; BLS lists an hourly figure only)

paths.title: Commercial dancer (music videos, tours, TV, award shows)
paths.what: You dance behind artists and on camera: music videos, concert tours, TV, commercials and live events.
paths.how_in: Agency representation is the main door, mostly in Los Angeles, plus taking class at the industry studios and being seen by choreographers who book jobs.
paths.training: Strong hip hop and commercial jazz, fast pickup, camera presence and freestyle. No degree needed. A reel and a headshot are your resume.
paths.pay: $24.80 an hour (BLS median for all dancers, May 2025)

paths.title: Broadway and national tours (musical theatre)
paths.what: You dance in the ensemble of a musical on Broadway or on a touring production, eight shows a week.
paths.how_in: Open calls and appointments listed on Playbill, Backstage and Actors' Equity; non-union tours are a common first step before joining Equity.
paths.training: Jazz, ballet, tap and contemporary, plus singing. Many come from BFA musical theatre or dance programs, but booking the job is what counts.
paths.pay: $24.80 an hour (BLS median for all dancers, May 2025)

paths.title: Theme park performer
paths.what: You perform in parades, stage shows and seasonal events at parks like Walt Disney World, Universal Orlando and SeaWorld.
paths.how_in: Each park posts its own auditions online; Orlando has more of these than almost anywhere, and seasonal shows (Halloween, holiday) are a common first booking.
paths.training: Versatile jazz, hip hop and musical theatre dance, quick pickup, stamina for outdoor heat. No degree needed.
paths.pay: $24.80 an hour (BLS median for all dancers, May 2025)

paths.title: Cruise ship performer
paths.what: You live on a ship for a contract of several months and dance in the production shows.
paths.how_in: Cruise lines hold open calls in many cities (including Orlando) and some take online submissions through a casting profile.
paths.training: Ballet, jazz, contemporary and hip hop, partnering and lifts; singing helps a lot. No degree needed. Most lines require 18 or older to be hired, some 20 or 21.
paths.pay: $24.80 an hour (BLS median for all dancers, May 2025)

paths.title: Cirque and specialty shows
paths.what: You dance in large-scale acrobatic or resident shows, often in Las Vegas or on tour.
paths.how_in: Apply online through the casting site with a video demo; Cirque keeps applicants on file and calls them for specific roles.
paths.training: Strong technique in one or more styles; acrobatics, tumbling or partnering are a big plus. Cirque requires applicants to be at least 18.
paths.pay: $24.80 an hour (BLS median for all dancers, May 2025)

paths.title: Choreographer (stage, concert, commercial)
paths.what: You create the movement for companies, shows, artists, videos or theme park productions.
paths.how_in: Almost everyone starts as a dancer, then builds a body of their own work: student pieces, showcases, festivals, assisting other choreographers.
paths.training: Dance experience plus composition classes. BLS says some employers prefer a bachelor's degree in dance or a related field.
paths.pay: $26.59 an hour (BLS median for choreographers, May 2025)

paths.title: Competition and studio choreographer
paths.what: You set solos, duets and group pieces for studios that compete, usually as a freelancer traveling between studios.
paths.how_in: Word of mouth: dancers with strong competition results and their own choreography get asked by studio owners, often starting with solos for younger dancers.
paths.training: Competition experience and a portfolio of pieces that placed. No degree required.
paths.pay: $26.59 an hour (BLS median for choreographers, May 2025)

paths.title: Dance teacher and studio owner
paths.what: You teach classes at a private studio, and later maybe run your own.
paths.how_in: Most start by assisting classes as teens (like you already do), then get their own classes; owning a studio means running a small business on top of teaching.
paths.training: Teaching experience and technique in the styles you teach. No license required for private studios. Business skills matter for owners.

paths.title: Convention faculty and assistant
paths.what: You travel with a dance convention on weekends, assisting a teacher onstage or teaching your own classes.
paths.how_in: Conventions pick from dancers they already know: scholarship winners and VIPs, then assistants, then faculty.
paths.training: A strong competition and convention track record and a teacher who vouches for you.

paths.title: K-12 dance teacher (certified) or college dance professor
paths.what: You teach dance in a public or private school, or in a college dance department.
paths.how_in: Earn a bachelor's (often in dance education), complete student teaching and pass your state's teaching exams; college teaching usually needs an MFA plus a professional career.
paths.training: Bachelor's degree and a state teaching certificate for public schools; an MFA is the usual degree for college faculty.
paths.pay: High school teachers: $72,040 a year (BLS median, May 2025). College art, drama and music teachers: $78,620 a year (BLS, May 2025).

paths.title: Dance/movement therapist
paths.what: You use movement as therapy to help people with mental, emotional and physical health.
paths.how_in: A master's from an ADTA-approved program (or ADTA's alternate route), then the R-DMT credential, then the advanced BC-DMT.
paths.training: Bachelor's (dance and psychology are good prep), then a required master's degree.

paths.title: Physical therapist / dance medicine
paths.what: You treat injuries and keep dancers and athletes moving; some PTs specialize in dancers.
paths.how_in: Bachelor's degree with science prerequisites, then a Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) program and a state license.
paths.training: DPT (doctoral) degree and a license in every state.

paths.title: Arts administration
paths.what: You run the business side of dance: company management, marketing, development, education programs, booking.
paths.how_in: Internships and entry-level jobs at companies and arts organizations; many former dancers move into these roles.
paths.training: Bachelor's degree is common; some get an MA in arts administration later.

paths.title: Film, TV and social content creator
paths.what: You build an audience with your own dance videos and choreography online, which can lead to brand deals, classes and bookings.
paths.how_in: Post consistently, find your style, collaborate with other creators; there is no audition, just the work.
paths.training: Filming and editing skills on top of dance. No degree needed.

paths.title: Fitness instructor (barre, Pilates, dance fitness)
paths.what: You teach group fitness or private sessions, a common side job and second career for dancers.
paths.how_in: Get certified in a method, then teach at studios or gyms; many dancers start this while still performing.
paths.training: High school diploma plus certification; BLS says most instructors hold a certification and need CPR/first aid.
paths.pay: $47,160 a year, or $22.67 an hour (BLS median, May 2025)

employers.name: Disney Auditions (Walt Disney World, Disney Live Entertainment)
employers.location: Orlando, FL (also Disneyland and international parks)
employers.min_age: Not stated on the main auditions page; each posting sets its own. News coverage has reported 16 for some Walt Disney World character roles, so check the posting.
employers.auditions: Auditions are posted on the Disney Auditions page with a filter by park and city; you need a Disney Auditions profile to sign up.
employers.why_john: The biggest dance employer in your backyard, and it casts all year.

employers.name: Disney Cruise Line
employers.location: Auditions listed by city on Disney Auditions
employers.min_age: Past mainstage dancer calls (2023, posted on Dance/NYC) said performers must be 18 or older.
employers.auditions: Listed on the same Disney Auditions page; past calls were in person only with a Disney Auditions profile and appointment.
employers.why_john: Mainstage shows are musical-theatre style, a fit for your jazz and contemporary.

employers.name: Universal Orlando Resort Entertainment
employers.min_age: The 2026 holiday parade call (reported by WDWNT) required 18 or older.
employers.auditions: Calls are posted on Universal's audition site for parades, Halloween Horror Nights and Epic Universe shows, usually with a video submission first.
employers.why_john: Seasonal shows like the holiday parade are a classic first professional booking in Orlando.

employers.name: SeaWorld Orlando and Busch Gardens Tampa Bay (United Parks)
employers.min_age: A 2026 seasonal SeaWorld Orlando dancer posting (third-party job board) said 18 or older.
employers.auditions: Seasonal live auditions (summer shows, Christmas shows) are posted under the Entertainment team on the United Parks careers site.
employers.why_john: Past calls asked for jazz, hip hop and jazz fusion, which is right in your lane.

employers.name: Royal Caribbean Productions
employers.min_age: "You must be 18 years of age or older to be hired." An Orlando call held at Orlando Ballet listed dancers as 18+.
employers.auditions: Auditions year round in over 60 cities; if you cannot attend, you can create a casting profile and submit online.
employers.why_john: They have held auditions right here at Orlando Ballet.

employers.name: Carnival Entertainment
employers.location: Auditions worldwide, including Orlando (Studio K, 2100 Orinoco Dr)
employers.min_age: Dancers Who Sing and Singers Who Dance: "at least 20 years old."
employers.auditions: Pre-registration open calls listed on the auditions page; an Orlando call for Dancers Who Sing was held October 13, 2026.
employers.why_john: They audition in Orlando, but you would need to be 20, so this is a later target.

employers.name: NCLH Creative Studios (Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings)
employers.min_age: Not stated on the auditions page; a 2025 Chicago call on Playbill said you must be 18 to apply.
employers.auditions: Runs online general submissions year round plus in-person dancer calls in rotating cities.
employers.why_john: Online submissions mean you can apply from Orlando once you are 18.

employers.name: Virgin Voyages
employers.min_age: Not stated on the careers page; a 2023 dancer call said 21+ to work onboard.
employers.auditions: Entertainment roles are posted on the shipboard careers page; past dancer calls asked for contemporary, commercial, hip hop and breaking.
employers.why_john: Their shows lean contemporary and commercial instead of classic revue.

employers.name: Cirque du Soleil
employers.min_age: "Applicants must be at least 18 years old."
employers.auditions: Apply online to a specific posting with a CV, headshot, full-body photo and video demo (12 minutes or less).
employers.why_john: Dance categories include contemporary, hip hop, tap and jazz, so you can build a file once you turn 18.

employers.name: Radio City Christmas Spectacular (Rockettes and ensemble)
employers.min_age: "All performers must be 18 years of age by the first day of rehearsals to be considered for casting."
employers.auditions: Open call once a year in spring at Radio City Music Hall with advance registration; 2026 registration is closed.
employers.why_john: The Rockettes are a women's line; the page does not say whether men can audition for the ensemble, so ask before you plan around it.

employers.name: NETworks (Broadway national tours)
employers.auditions: The jobs page lists crew, music and tour management roles; performer calls for tours show up on boards like Playbill and Backstage.
employers.why_john: Tours are how most dancers first work in Broadway shows outside New York.

employers.name: Orlando Magic: The 407
employers.auditions: Co-ed hip hop crew launched in 2019 to replace the Magic Dancers, cast through an open call announced by the team; no current call found.
employers.why_john: A home-team co-ed hip hop crew that takes men.

employers.name: Memphis Hustle Hype Crew (NBA G League)
employers.min_age: "performers ages 18 and up of all backgrounds"
employers.auditions: Yearly open tryouts in September with a free clinic the week before.
employers.why_john: A confirmed co-ed hip hop team, a model for what sports entertainment jobs for men look like.

employers.name: Orlando Ballet (company)
employers.auditions: Send a video and materials for review, then register for an in-person audition through Dance Apply; right now all company and second company spots are filled. No audition fee.
employers.why_john: Your hometown professional company, and it does contemporary repertory too.

employers.name: Orlando Ballet II and Trainee programs
employers.min_age: OBII and Trainee: "Age 16-21 by Audition only"
employers.auditions: In-person auditions in May and August before each school year, or a video audition until December 31.
employers.why_john: You are in the age window right now, and it is in Orlando; it is ballet-heavy, so your classical has to be strong.

employers.name: Dance Theatre of Orlando
employers.location: Orlando, FL (Marshall Ellis Theatre, 1300 La Quinta Dr)
employers.auditions: Small contemporary company (formerly ME Dance) with company members, apprentices and trainees per past show listings; no public audition page found, so contact them directly.
employers.why_john: A local contemporary company where an apprentice or trainee spot is realistic.

employers.name: Central Florida Ballet
employers.min_age: Studio Company: ages 7 through 17. Nutcracker: freelance professionals and students ages 5 and up (per its Nutcracker audition page).
employers.auditions: Studio Company and Nutcracker auditions have been held in August.
employers.why_john: Mostly a training program, but Nutcracker casting takes freelancers, which is stage time close to home.

employers.name: Ailey II
employers.auditions: Invitation only, mainly from students in The Ailey School's full-time programs.
employers.why_john: The way in is The Ailey School first, see the next entry.

employers.name: The Ailey School Professional Division (Certificate Program)
employers.min_age: Certificate Program: ages 17 to 23 who have completed secondary school.
employers.auditions: Audition tour runs January to February; 2027 dates are announced in October. Video auditions are not currently accepted.
employers.why_john: You fit the age range and could audition this winter for fall 2027, right after graduation.

employers.name: Philadanco D/2
employers.auditions: Yearly apprentice company audition in January ($15 cash fee in 2026).
employers.why_john: You can audition at 17, and it is a real performing second company (about 25 shows a year).

employers.name: Dallas Black Dance Theatre: Encore!
employers.auditions: Applications (headshot, resume, dance photos, reel) due in February, then invitation-only in-person auditions in March.
employers.why_john: Seeks early career dancers with modern and classical training.

employers.name: Giordano II (Giordano Dance Chicago)
employers.min_age: Not on the current page; a 2018 call required age 22, so check.
employers.auditions: Yearly audition (the 2025 one was in NYC in February) with reel, headshot and resume; positions are paid.
employers.why_john: America's original jazz company, a strong fit for your jazz.

employers.name: Hubbard Street Dance Chicago
employers.auditions: Hubbard Street 2 was suspended in December 2016; the training path now runs through summer intensive auditions held each winter.
employers.why_john: A top contemporary company; the summer intensive is the way to get seen.

employers.name: Graham 2 (Martha Graham)
employers.auditions: Pre-professional company drawn from advanced Martha Graham School students; admission by audition or faculty recommendation.
employers.why_john: A modern-dance second company if you go the NYC training route.

employers.name: Complexions Contemporary Ballet (Complexions Academy)
employers.auditions: All academy programs need an in-person or video audition through DanceApply; company members have come up through the intensives, some as apprentices.
employers.why_john: Contemporary ballet with big partnering, and the academy is the pipeline.

employers.name: MSA Agency
employers.auditions: No open calls listed; submit through the Talent Seeking Representation form with headshot, resume and videos.
employers.why_john: A major dance agency; you can submit from anywhere.

employers.name: Go 2 Talent Agency
employers.auditions: Online submission form; the site says no auditions or class observations are scheduled right now.
employers.why_john: A boutique agency that only reps dancers and choreographers.

employers.name: Bloc Agency
employers.location: Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta, Toronto, Vancouver, London
employers.auditions: No submission policy found on the site; check each city office page.

employers.name: Clear Talent Group
employers.auditions: No submission policy found on the site.

employers.name: CESD Talent
employers.auditions: Fill out the online form for on-camera and dance representation; the roster includes teens.
employers.why_john: Has a teens category, so it is one agency that works with dancers your age.

employers.name: JUMP Dance Convention (DanceOne)
employers.location: Touring; The Dance Awards 2027 in Orlando (June 26 to July 3) and Las Vegas
employers.min_age: VIP Senior division: 16-19 (age as of January 1, 2027)
employers.auditions: VIP scholarship audition at each regional workshop; winners and runners-up qualify for Best Dancer at The Dance Awards.
employers.why_john: VIP is your road to The Dance Awards, and the Orlando finals are local.

employers.name: RADIX Dance Convention
employers.min_age: Protégé Senior: 16-19; dancers 20 and older are not eligible for scholarships
employers.auditions: Protégé scholarship audition class at each full workshop.
employers.why_john: Another scholarship ladder that convention faculty watch.

employers.name: New York City Dance Alliance (NYCDA)
employers.auditions: Outstanding Dancer programs at regionals and nationals, plus a College Scholarship Audition through the NYCDA Foundation.
employers.why_john: The College Scholarship Audition can turn into money for a BFA.

employers.name: DanceOne (JUMP, NUVO, 24 Seven, The Dance Awards) company jobs
employers.auditions: Staff jobs posted on the careers page; current openings include Orlando tech and warehouse roles and a remote junior social media role.
employers.why_john: The company behind the conventions you compete at has jobs in Orlando, a way into the industry off the stage.

boards.what: Universal's own casting calls for parades, Halloween Horror Nights and park shows.
